verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The market empties out and the pigeons take the square.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text: An empty bottle rolls across the platform, going nowhere fast.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Streetlight flickers on early,
catching a moth mid-turn --
someone upstairs closes their window
against the coming dark.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off in the next room --
steam finds the crack under the door
and disappears before it means anything.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A dog barks twice at nothing,
then settles back to sleep --
the whole street holding its breath
for no reason at all.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone's left the porch light burning
for a guest who isn't coming --
the moths have made their peace with that,
circling anyway.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Down at the corner, the bus shelter
holds a stranger's forgotten umbrella --
rain hasn't come in weeks
but someone still might need it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The clock in the hallway loses a minute every day --
nobody's fixed it in years,
we've just learned to arrive a little early
for everything that matters.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The mailbox flag stays up
long after the letters are gone --
some habits outlive
what they were ever for.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The garden hose is coiled just so,
though nothing's grown here since spring --
some hands just need
a shape to return to.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A key still waits beneath the mat
though the locks were changed last fall --
the door recognizes nothing,
but the foot still pauses there.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The porch light flips on by itself at dusk --
no one taught it grief,
it just keeps doing
the one thing it was built for.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The clock upstairs runs ten minutes fast,
nobody bothers to fix it now --
we've learned to subtract the difference
without even thinking of why.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The mail still comes addressed to both names --
the carrier doesn't know,
or maybe knows too well
which silence to leave unsorted.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The dog waits by the wrong door still,
nose pressed to hinges that don't open --
some mornings we let him wait a little longer,
just to watch him hope.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The garden's gone to seed on purpose --
we tell ourselves it's wildness, not neglect,
and something in the tangle
almost believes us back.
